problem.canonical_statement: Erdos problem 289 (erdosproblems.com/289, OPEN): Is it true that, for all sufficiently large k, there exist finite intervals I_1, ..., I_k of consecutive integers in N, pairwise distinct, not overlapping or adjacent, with |I_i| >= 2 for 1 <= i <= k, such that 1 = sum over i of sum over n in I_i of 1/n?
definitions: interval I = [a,b]: the consecutive integers a, a+1, ..., b inclusive; |I| = b - a + 1
non-adjacent: for sorted intervals, next.a >= prev.b + 2 (a gap of at least one integer)
a >= 2 for every interval (1/1 excluded by the reciprocal-sum context; a=1 gives sum >= 1 trivially and is treated per source convention as excluded)
the equation is EXACT rational equality, not approximation
quantifier order: for all sufficiently large k, THERE EXIST intervals (existence per k, uniform threshold)
permitted_background: harmonic partial sum asymptotics H(b)-H(a-1) ~ ln(b/(a-1))
exact Fraction arithmetic as WORLD verifier (machine-checked)

close_branch_A.statement: AFFIRMATIVE: prove for all k >= K0 (explicit or existence of K0) a valid k-interval decomposition of 1 exists
must_determine: a construction scheme valid for every sufficiently large k
proof the scheme's sums are exactly 1 with all constraints

close_branch_B.statement: NEGATIVE: prove infinitely many k admit NO valid k-interval decomposition of 1
must_determine: an obstruction argument (parity/valuation/measure) ruling out infinitely many k

non_results: decompositions for finitely many specific k without a scheme for all large k
approximate sums (any inequality in place of exact equality)
decompositions using length-1 intervals or adjacent intervals
density or almost-all-k statements when the problem demands all sufficiently large k
a reduction to another open unit-fraction conjecture of comparable strength
invariants_that_must_survive_every_refor: the quantifier: all sufficiently large k
known_traps: adjacency violations (e.g. [2,3] and [4,5] are ADJACENT and illegal) - killed run-15 attempts
sum drift: partial-fraction splits that break interval structure
1/n = 1/(n+1) + 1/(n(n+1)) produces NON-interval terms; interval structure must be restored
verifying k intervals but claiming all large k (sampled-to-universal, MSL L-law)
the empty/trivial k=1 case: no single interval of length >= 2 starting >= 2 sums to exactly 1 in any small range searched (starts < 120, exhaustive)
